aws-dva-c02-s1.1-08.reason: ambiguous: the old ordering claim with a hedge could be defended as True before throttling is seen. The verifier's False wording would be a compound statement (true retry half, false initial-request half), so the card now states the single documented fact as True. This also moves 1.1 from 4/6 to 5/5. Source: 'Unlike standard mode, adaptive mode can delay or block the initial request, not just retries, when throttling is detected.' (final: keep)
aws-dva-c02-s1.1-08.statement: Adaptive retry mode in an AWS SDK rate-limits initial requests too once it detects throttling.
aws-dva-c02-s1.1-08.explanation: Adaptive mode adds a per-client rate limiter driven by throttling responses, so it can hold back a first attempt, not only a retry. Standard mode never delays the initial request.

Statement and answer are unchanged. (final: keep)
aws-dva-c02-s2.1-01.statement: An Amazon Cognito user pool issues AWS access keys after a user signs in.
aws-dva-c02-s2.1-01.explanation: After a successful sign-in, a Cognito user pool returns an ID token, an access token and a refresh token. Apps can exchange those tokens for temporary AWS credentials in a separate step.
aws-dva-c02-s2.1-01.misconception: Cognito user pool sign-in supplies credentials for direct AWS API calls.

source.title: Understanding user pool JSON web tokens (JWTs)

aws-dva-c02-s2.2-06.reason: ambiguous: the old statement made S3 the actor that checks kms:Decrypt and implied a check on every download (S3 Bucket Keys skip repeat KMS calls). It now states the caller's requirement. Source: 'To download an object encrypted with an AWS KMS key, you need kms:Decrypt permissions for the key' and 'Amazon S3 sends the encrypted data key to AWS KMS in a Decrypt request.' (final: fixed)
aws-dva-c02-s2.2-06.statement: Amazon S3 GetObject on an SSE-KMS object needs the caller to hold kms:Decrypt on its KMS key.
aws-dva-c02-s2.2-06.explanation: A caller needs kms:Decrypt on the object's KMS key as well as s3:GetObject, because that key protects the data key S3 stored with the object. Without it, the download is denied.

source.title: Using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS)

aws-dva-c02-s3.3-07.reason: explanation_error: the old explanation said CloudFormation 'skips' the dependent resource, which implies the rest of the stack deploys normally. In practice an unguarded Ref fails validation. No official page names that error, so the new explanation keeps only what the Condition attribute note supports ('If a resource with a condition isn't created, any resources that depend on that resource aren't created either, regardless of their own conditions'). That wording is true under both the documented and the observed behaviour. Statement and answer are unchanged. (final: fixed)
aws-dva-c02-s3.3-07.statement: AWS CloudFormation creates a resource that uses Ref to point to a resource whose condition evaluates to false.
aws-dva-c02-s3.3-07.explanation: CloudFormation creates a conditional resource only when its condition is true. A resource that depends on an uncreated resource can't be created either, whatever its own condition says.
aws-dva-c02-s3.3-07.misconception: A true resource condition permits creation despite a referenced dependency being excluded by its condition.

aws-dva-c02-s3.3-12.statement: AWS CloudFormation ValidateTemplate verifies that an EC2 instance's KeyName names an existing key pair.
aws-dva-c02-s3.3-12.explanation: ValidateTemplate checks that the template is valid JSON or YAML. Whether a named EC2 key pair exists comes to light when CloudFormation creates or updates the stack.
aws-dva-c02-s3.3-12.misconception: Template validation verifies that resource property values identify existing resources in the target environment.
